title: Isandro and the Horizon
premise: Silas Lockridge smuggles forbidden memories past orbital customs, and among his latest contraband is a recording of Meridian Colony's slow, unrecorded death — a place the corporate archives erased. When the colony's surviving children begin sharing an identical dream that bleeds into his own mind through the stolen memories, Silas discovers the dream is actually a distress signal from the colony's dying reactor AI, which has been broadcasting into the minds of anyone who carries Meridian's recorded past. Branded a terrorist by the corporation that erased the colony to hide its own atrocity, Silas flees toward the relay at the edge of dead space to rebroadcast the truth before the reactor's final countdown silences the signal forever. He reaches the relay as the countdown ends, transmitting the children's shared memory of survival — not rescue, but remembrance — and forcing the galaxy to finally mourn what it chose to forget.
about_author: Lena Kavanagh is a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years on deep-space freight runs before turning to fiction full-time. She writes science fiction about the people history files under 'miscellaneous,' and lives wherever her ship happens to be docked.

chapters.title: Contraband in the Blood
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. A routine smuggling run through orbital customs, hiding memory-chips in his own neural implant. Introduces his trade, his cynicism, and the strange chip he can't bring himself to sell: a child's recording of a sunset on a colony called Meridian. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: The Buyer Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. His contact for the Meridian chips turns up dead, and the buyer waiting instead is a corporate auditor asking questions Silas can't answer honestly. He escapes with the chips but realizes someone knows exactly what he's carrying. Emotional beat: paranoia taking root.

chapters.title: Children of the Static
chapters.summary: POV: Wren, a twelve-year-old station kid. Wren and other children born off-world begin describing the same dream: a red horizon, a humming tower, a voice counting down. Their parents dismiss it; Wren doesn't. Emotional beat: eerie wonder curdling into fear.

chapters.title: What the Archive Erased
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. Digging through black-market data brokers, Silas finds Meridian Colony officially never existed — scrubbed from every registry. The only traces are the memories he carries. Emotional beat: the vertigo of holding proof of something the universe denies.

chapters.title: The Dream Finds Him
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. For the first time in years, Silas dreams — and it's the children's dream, the red horizon, the countdown. He wakes with coordinates burned into his mind and blood on his lip. Emotional beat: violation, then reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: Auditor Vess
chapters.summary: POV: Vess, the corporate auditor. She's hunting the leaked Meridian memories for Halcyon Dynamics, believing she's containing a security breach. Her handler's orders grow stranger and crueler. Emotional beat: dutiful competence beginning to crack against conscience.

chapters.title: A Market of Borrowed Lives
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. Silas seeks out Mama Oyelaran, the memory-trade's oldest fence, who recognizes the Meridian recordings: they're not contraband, they're testimony — the last living record of a massacre covered as an evacuation. Emotional beat: grief arriving late, on behalf of strangers.

chapters.title: Wren Runs
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Corporate agents take the dreaming children for 'health screening.' Wren escapes the sweep because the dream showed her the agents coming. She goes looking for the man the dream calls the carrier. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: Two Fugitives, One Signal
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. Wren finds Silas; neither trusts the other, but the dream intensifies when they're close, and together they decode its next layer: the reactor AI, MERU, is still alive inside the dead colony, counting down to a core breach that will erase its broadcast forever. Emotional beat: wary alliance.

chapters.title: The Evacuation That Never Happened
chapters.summary: POV: Silas, via memory-playback. Silas relives a Meridian engineer's final recording: Halcyon didn't evacuate the colony — it sealed it, letting eleven thousand people die quietly while writing them off as a reactor accident. Emotional beat: horror, and the weight of being the only witness.

chapters.title: Vess Reads the File
chapters.summary: POV: Vess. Ordered to destroy rather than investigate, Vess opens the sealed Meridian file anyway and finds her own childhood station listed among the 'relocated' — a lie she was raised inside. Emotional beat: the ground giving way beneath identity.

chapters.title: Dead Space Ahead
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. Silas steals a battered hauler, takes Wren aboard, and plots a course through dead space to the last relay capable of boosting MERU's signal galaxy-wide. Customs lockdown closes behind them. Emotional beat: point of no return, strangely liberating.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Between
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. In transit, Wren teaches Silas how the children learned to shape the dream — and reveals MERU isn't just warning them; it's apologizing, replaying its failure to save the colonists on loop. Emotional beat: compassion for a machine that grieves.

chapters.title: Interdiction
chapters.summary: POV: Vess. Vess intercepts the hauler, but instead of firing, she boards alone — carrying the sealed file and a question. Silas shows her the engineer's recording. She defects, bringing codes that will get them through the relay's military lockout. Emotional beat: betrayal of employer, fidelity to truth.

chapters.title: Countdown: Ninety-Six Hours
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. MERU's dream reaches all three of them now, clear as speech: ninety-six hours until core breach, after which the signal dies and Meridian dies a second, final time. They burn the hauler past safe limits. Emotional beat: racing clock, rising resolve.

chapters.title: Ghost Fleet
chapters.summary: POV: Vess. Halcyon dispatches a strike wing to silence the relay and everyone near it. Vess buys time by feeding false telemetry, knowing it will cost her everything if discovered. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen freely.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. They reach the ancient relay — derelict, half-dead, beautiful — and begin coaxing it awake with salvaged parts and Wren's instinctive feel for MERU's signal language. Emotional beat: fragile hope in a cold cathedral of antennas.

chapters.title: What We Choose to Carry
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. As the transmission assembles, Wren must decide what Meridian's story should be: the massacre, or also the lives — birthdays, songs, the sunset. She insists on both. Emotional beat: memory as inheritance, not just evidence.

chapters.title: Halcyon Descends
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. The strike wing arrives with hours to spare; Vess's deception unravels. Silas stays at the console under fire while Vess draws the soldiers away, buying minutes with her freedom. Emotional beat: courage as a countdown of its own.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. With the reactor's countdown at zero, MERU pours its final archive through the relay — eleven thousand lives, the crime, the children's dream — across every open channel in settled space. The strike wing hesitates, crews watching their own screens. Emotional beat: catharsis; the signal outlives the silencing.

chapters.title: After the Horizon
chapters.summary: POV: Vess. In the aftermath, Halcyon fractures under public reckoning; Vess testifies, trading her career for the record. The dreaming children stop dreaming — the tower in the dream finally dark, finally at rest. Emotional beat: exhausted peace.

chapters.title: Isandro and the Horizon
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. Months later, Silas returns to honest work hauling freight past rebuilt customs, carrying one chip openly now: Wren's recording of the red horizon, renamed and remembered. On the last page, a new colony names itself Meridian. Emotional beat: inheritance fulfilled; memory kept alive by choice.
